candidate.answerReason: The maximum is seven 5-cent coins, and the minimum is two coins worth 25 and 10 cents. Their difference is 5.

methods.label: Bound each extreme and attain it
methods.explanation:
Every coin is worth at least \(5\) cents, so a payment of \(35\) cents can use at most \(35\div5=7\) coins. Seven \(5\)-cent coins pay exactly \(35\) cents, so this maximum is attainable.

One coin cannot pay \(35\) cents because the largest available coin is worth \(25\) cents. Two coins can pay the amount: \(25+10=35\). Thus the smallest number of coins is \(2\).

The requested difference is \(7-2=\boxed{5}\), choice E.
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary coin values, division, and explicit payments to establish both extremes.

review.mathematicalCheck: The minimum coin value bounds the count above by seven, attained by seven nickels. No single available coin pays 35 cents, while a quarter and dime do, establishing the minimum of two. The difference is five.
